## Context

Memzy is a multi-student web app for spaced-repetition vocabulary training, built for a
Latin teacher to run with her class. This requirement is the **north star**: a high-level
architecture outline that fixes the major technology and data-model decisions.

## Decisions

| # | Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|----------|--------|-----------|
| D1 | Backend stack | **Django 5.x (Python)** | Built-in auth, admin as a day-one teacher console. |
| D2 | Scheduling library | **py-fsrs** | Same algorithm as the canonical Rust crate. |

## Acceptance criteria

Architectural invariants — any implementation claiming to satisfy this north star must hold these:

- [ ] The only component importing the FSRS library is a single `scheduling` service
      module; all review scheduling goes through it (D2 swap-ability).
- [ ] No `Student` record stores a real name or email; students authenticate by
      nickname + access code only (D7, GDPR).
- [ ] Every teacher-owned entity carries an `owner` FK to a Teacher (D9 future-proofing).

Pilot success definition (what "north star reached for the experiment" means):

- [ ] 2–3 classes of students can each log in with a nickname + code and complete daily
      review sessions on a phone browser.
- [ ] FSRS scheduling demonstrably spaces reviews (due dates advance correctly with ratings).

## Notes

- **Why Django over Flask-Security-Too**: for a nicknames-only, teacher-provisioned,
  single-teacher pilot, the email-verification machinery is out of scope.
